subject: Dedicated capacity proposal: scaling staircase, spot tranches, and autoscale policy for ZephyrAI
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Ng <sarah.ng@zephyr.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal: scaling staircase, spot tranches, and autoscale policy for ZephyrAI

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached are the demand profile and the sizing sheet we pulled together from your telemetry (zephyr_demand_profile_Q2-2027.pdf, sizing-sheet-zephyr.csv). Based on the traffic shapes and the latency SLO you shared (p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 350ms for interactive generation), here’s a pragmatic Dedicated kickoff proposal focused on predictable baseline plus safe burst lanes: 

Summary proposal (initial committed configuration)
- Baseline reserved: 4 x A100-80GB GPUs (pinned pool) for steady-state inference (handles 90% of normal demand with caching and batching).
- Shoulder reserve: 2 additional A100 GPUs in a warm shoulder for predictable day-to-day spikes (capacity to absorb sustained 20–40% uplift).
- Burst/ephemeral slab: up to 4 ephemeral GPUs (prewarmed) available for short peaks; ephemeral slab runs as higher-cost transient capacity with automatic fallback to smaller model variant when exhaust.
- Spot tranche: recommend 20–25% of burst capacity as spot/preemptible instances to reduce unit cost; spot will be used only for non-critical batch reranks and background jobs unless explicitly allowed for inference.

Autoscale policy (proposal)
- Staircase thresholds: baseline -> shoulder threshold at 65% p95 utilization; shoulder->burst at 85% p95 utilization sustained for 90s.
- Scale step: add 1 GPU per step, cooldown 60s between adds, graceful drain 45s on scale-in.
- Prewarm policy: keep 1 prewarmed slot ready when expected traffic probability > 30% (based on your schedule); prewarm time target: <= 90s.
- Eviction/degeneration: when ephemeral slab exhausted, requests route to fallback model variant (quantized 4-bit) with explicit header so app can surface degradation.

Contractual/ops notes
- We can include a burst-credit pool (X hours/month) that converts to transient capacity credits for unplanned spikes.
- Billing: baseline dedicated priced at committed rate; ephemeral/spot billed at usage rate with 95th percentile smoothing for multi-day spikes (TBD).

Next steps
1) Can you confirm expected peak QPS and a 7-day hourly traffic sample (if you can attach the weekly traffic CSV that would help)?
2) If this looks directionally correct I’ll loop in Karthik and Neha to translate into a SOW amendment with the exact SLA/burst-credit language.

Attachment: zephyr_demand_profile_Q2-2027.pdf, sizing-sheet-zephyr.csv

Best,

Rachel — nice write-up. A few practical adjustments from an ops/runtime perspective: 

1) GPU packing and concurrency
- For interactive workloads with short sequences, target 6–8 concurrent streams per A100-80 with batching tuned to 12–16 tokens avg. That lowers the node count vs naive estimates but keeps p95 latency tight. Add a conservative buffer of ~10% for scheduling jitter.

2) Spot tranching specifics
- I recommend we limit spot to background reranks and non-blocking reroutes by default. If Zephyr wants to use spot for lower-cost inference, include an opt-in flag in SOW so we can add a 15-min grace to avoid user-facing preemptions.

3) Prewarm and ephemeral semantics
- Prewarm warmup time measured in our infra is ~60–120s depending on model size. We should prespecify a minimum prewarm SLA (e.g., 90s) and allow Zephyr to request a priority prewarm window on known events.

4) Autoscale wording for SOW
- Add explicit scale-in damping: min node lifetime 5 minutes before eviction to avoid oscillation.
- Define billing for burst: first 30 minutes of an unplanned burst charged at committed rate, thereafter usage-rate for ephemeral. Also propose a monthly burst-credit bucket (e.g., 40 GPU-hours) that auto-applies to ephemeral usage before usage-rate billing kicks in.

5) Failure modes and fallbacks
- If shoulder + burst exhausted, system returns a short header ("X-Redwood-Fallback: quant4") so Zephyr can log and optionally surface a friendly message.

I attached a quick spreadsheet with autoscale knobs and a cost sensitivity tab — autoscale-suggestion.xlsx — that you can share with the customer. Marissa/Neha: flag anything legal/commercial that must be prespecified (credits, notice windows, etc.).

-Karthik
Director, Inference Products — Redwood Inference

Sarah — looping you and ops together with the internal team. Below is a concise set of agreed/confirmed items and proposed contractual language we can put into an SOW amendment or an addendum. Please tell me if anything looks off and I’ll open the SOW edit.

Operational summary (agreed/high-confidence points)
- Committed baseline: 4 x A100-80GB GPUs (reserved)
- Shoulder reserve: +2 A100 GPUs (warm)
- Burst/ephemeral: up to 4 ephemeral GPUs (prewarmed on demand)
- Spot tranche: initial default set to 25% of burst capacity (i.e., 1 of 4 ephemeral GPUs), used for non-critical background tasks unless Zephyr opts-in for inference at reduced SLA.

Autoscale staircase (explicit thresholds)
- Baseline -> Shoulder: sustained p95 utilization >= 65% for 90s
- Shoulder -> Burst: sustained p95 utilization >= 85% for 90s
- Scale step size: +1 GPU; scale-in min lifetime 5m, scale-in cooldown 120s
- Prewarm SLAs: target warmup <= 90s; priority prewarm windows negotiable in advance.

Billing and burst credits (contract-ready language suggestion)
"Customer will receive a monthly burst-credit allocation equal to 40 GPU-hours. Burst-credits are consumed by ephemeral GPU usage before pay-as-you-go rates apply. For unplanned bursts exceeding the burst-credit bucket, ephemeral usage will be billed at the pay-as-you-go rate published in Appendix A. The first 30 minutes of an unplanned burst are billed at the committed rate as a protection against frequent oscillation."

Spot preemption handling
- Redwood will maintain a 2-tier fallback: (1) shift traffic to shoulder/reserved pool when capacity is available; (2) when unavailable, route to a lower-cost quantized model variant with explicit response header so customer telemetry can distinguish fallback events.
- Typical preemption windows in us-west-2 historically: median daily preemption events for spot pools at 6–12% but variable; Redwood will not use spot for interactive inference unless customer explicitly opts in.

Next steps
1) Rachel to produce a cost sensitivity table (committed vs ephemeral at 1x/2x/3x peaks) and attach a draft SOW amendment.
2) Zephyr to confirm whether they want an opt-in for spot-inference (yes/no) and to confirm the June 18 marketing event spike (expected 3x).
3) Once Zephyr confirms, Redwood will publish an SOW addendum and a DocuSign link for signature.

Attachments: autoscale-suggestion.xlsx, sizing-sheet-zephyr.csv

DocuSign (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/zephyr-sow-amendment

Thanks all — let me know if you'd like a quick 20-min ops sync next week to walk the thresholds and the cost table.
